title: vulnsuite Target Contract
description: A portable, reproducible description of a vulnerable system and its patched counterpart. Built and run by vulnsuite on any device with Docker.

then.description: A source or build base builds every state from its own source: a per-state image (and the digest pinning it) applies only to kind: image.
On an image base an overlay dest is a path in the image, so it must be absolute.
A variant discriminates a member within its group, so it needs one.

id.description: Unique target id; also a Docker repository path component, so no leading, trailing or doubled '.'/'-'.

summary.description: One-line description; must not be blank.

vuln_refs.description: CVE or GHSA ids, or a PREFIX-ID for simulations / misconfigurations with no CVE (community templates use VS-...). The PREFIX-ID form is 2-8 upper-case letters other than CVE and GHSA (the pattern spells that out without a lookahead), so a malformed CVE-/GHSA- id is rejected rather than taken as a generic ref.

added.description: ISO date the target was first added (YYYY-MM-DD).

updated.description: ISO date of the last change to this target's metadata or states (YYYY-MM-DD); bump it whenever CVE facts, versions, or probes change. Defaults to `added` when never updated.

detected_by.description: scanner template ids this target reproduces the fingerprint of, e.g. nuclei:laravel-env

detection.description: scanner = reproduces a real scanner template's fingerprint (name it in detected_by); custom-only = no public template exists, validate with your own probes

fidelity.description: real = runs the genuine affected software (preferred); simulated = a hand-written stand-in (only for bare-OS/device/protocol flaws with no reproducible image/source)

verification.description: verified (the default) = someone ran every state on a host that can run it and verify passed; unverified = the contract is statically sound but nobody has run it yet (e.g. it needs hardware no maintainer has). `vulnsuite validate` warns on unverified (an error under -strict), and `list -unverified` selects such targets.

verified_on.description: Evidence of the last run in which every listed state verified ok, one per host and image platform: a mapping for a single run, a list for runs on several hosts (no two on the same host and platform). Written by `vulnsuite stamp`, not by hand.

class.description: finding class(es) (taxonomy v2), orthogonal to the product surface (the top directory level): vuln = a tracked software vulnerability (usually a CVE); misconfig = an insecure configuration; exposure = data/interface reachable that should not be; default-login = default/weak credentials; weak-crypto = weak or broken cryptography. `vulnsuite list --class` filters on it.

group.description: Variant-family handle. Targets sharing a group are variants of one vulnerability; a selector naming the group resolves to its primary, and -variants expands to all members. A lone target with a group is a nickname for its id.

primary.description: Marks the canonical member of a group. Exactly one member of a multi-member group must set it; a single-member group needs none.

variant.description: Discriminates this member within its group (e.g. waf-evasion); unique within the group.

disclosed.description: optional public-disclosure date (YYYY-MM-DD), a real calendar date (vulnsuite also rejects e.g. 2021-02-30); drives the list --year/--since filters and a timeline view, falling back to the CVE-id year when unset.

base.description: The reusable, content-addressed foundation. Templates sharing a base reuse one built image.

commit.description: Pinned commit -- an RC or unreleased vulnerable revision. Must be a full 40-character (or 64-character SHA-256) commit id: `validate` reports a branch or tag as unpinned-base and an abbreviated id as short-commit.

dockerfile.description: Dockerfile path inside the build context. Relative to the template folder: not absolute, no .. segments, no control characters; a symlink must resolve inside the folder.

context.description: Folder inside the template with a Dockerfile + source (e.g. a Python/Go socket sim). Relative to the template folder: not absolute, no .. segments, no control characters; a symlink must resolve inside the folder.

dockerfile.description: Dockerfile path inside the build context. Relative to the template folder: not absolute, no .. segments, no control characters; a symlink must resolve inside the folder.

publish.description: Also publish this secondary port on the host and include it in scanner target lists. The primary port is always published; this opts an additional port in.

healthcheck.description: when the target is ready: an http check or a tcp check, not both

timeout.description: how long to wait for the target to become ready (default 60s): greater than 0 and at most 24h (vulnsuite enforces the upper bound)

sidecars.description: Helper containers started next to the target. Each runs a prebuilt image (pin it with digest; `validate`: unpinned-sidecar) or an image built from a context in the template (build), never both; under emulation they run on the target's platform.

name.description: Part of the sidecar's container name and its network alias (and of a built sidecar's image tag).

build.description: Build the sidecar's image from a context in the template, like a kind: build base, instead of running a prebuilt image. The image is tagged vulnsuite/<id>:sidecar-<name>-<hash> by content (Dockerfile path, context, build_args), so it is pinned by construction and never rebuilt when unchanged.

context.description: Folder inside the template with the sidecar's Dockerfile and files. Relative to the template folder: not absolute, no .. segments, no control characters; a symlink must resolve inside the folder.

dockerfile.description: Dockerfile path inside the build context (default Dockerfile). Not absolute, no .. segments, no control characters; a symlink must resolve inside the context.

then.description: A built sidecar takes no digest (its tag is its content hash), and its name is part of that tag.

cap_add.description: Linux capabilities to grant on top of the default set, e.g. CAP_SYS_CHROOT

cap_drop.description: Linux capabilities to drop, e.g. ['ALL'] for a hand-audited paranoid target (then add back what the image needs via cap_add)

devices.description: Host devices to pass through to the container (consent-gated by run -allow-host-access). Only /dev/kvm, /dev/net/tun, /dev/fuse, /dev/vhost-net, /dev/vhost-vsock and /dev/dri/cardN|renderDN are allowed; raw disk/memory and other host devices are rejected

sanitizer.description: Where a sanitizer-instrumented target writes its reports, for sequence expect_sanitizer steps. Point log_path at it (ASAN_OPTIONS=...:log_path=<log_dir>/asan). Not part of the image hash.

log_dir.description: Absolute, canonical directory in the target (no trailing /, no //, no . or .. segments, not /), a plain path: letters, digits and . _ @ % + = : , / -.

requires.description: What the container host must provide; the tooling preflights it and skips or emulates with a reason.

arch.description: host CPU arch(es) that run natively; empty = any

emulation.description: allow qemu emulation when the host arch is not in arch (default true)

cpu_flags.description: CPU feature flags the daemon's machine must have, as /proc/cpuinfo names them (x86 `flags`, arm64 `Features`), e.g. [avx512f, avx512bw, avx512vbmi, bmi2]. Read from the daemon (not the CLI host) only when a selected target sets it; a target whose flags are missing, or cannot be read, is skipped. Implies no emulation: qemu does not provide them.

run.description: a /bin/sh -c command run in the target's image (no network, no capabilities) after its image is built or pulled and before anything starts; exit 0 = the host can run the target

reason.description: the skip reason when run exits non-zero, e.g. needs AVX-512 VBMI

timeout.description: bound on run (default 30s): greater than 0 and at most 24h (vulnsuite enforces the upper bound); running out fails the target rather than skipping it

probe.description: Generic host check for what no dedicated field covers (kernel version, cgroup v2, a sysctl, a device). A non-zero exit skips the target with reason, never fails it; -ignore-requires does not run it.

then.description: A digest pins the state's image override; without image it would be ignored and the state would run the base image.

image.description: Per-state image override (reuse-if-matches): e.g. patched = a newer tag. Only for kind: image bases; a source or build base rejects it. Pin it with digest (`validate`: unpinned-state-image). Part of the content hash of an overlay build.

digest.description: Digest pinning the state's image override (kind: image bases only).

patch.description: Git patch applied to a source base to reach this state. Relative to the template folder: not absolute, no .. segments, no control characters; a symlink must resolve inside the folder.

src.description: Template file to bake in. Relative to the template folder: not absolute, no .. segments, no control characters; a symlink must resolve inside the folder.

dest.description: Absolute path in the image (image base) or a path in the build context (source/build base), naming the file. A plain path: letters, digits and . _ @ % + = : , / -; no whitespace, quotes, $ or control characters; no .. segments; not the root; no trailing / or /. (an image base would copy into that directory, a source/build base would write a file).

mode.description: File mode, set in the build context (no RUN chmod, so it works on non-root and shell-less bases). Part of the content hash.

environment.description: Baked into built images as ENV lines and passed at run time. Names are plain variable names; values may not contain control characters.

sidecars.description: Per-state sidecar image overrides, keyed by sidecar name (e.g. the patched version on every node of a multi-node target). An override swaps a sidecar's image, or runs an image in place of a built sidecar's build. Pin each image with digest (`validate`: unpinned-sidecar).

header_matches.description: response header name -> regex the value must match (case-insensitive name)

header_absent.description: response header names that must NOT be present

port.description: Target a non-primary container port (default: the primary port).

closed.description: Assert the port is NOT open (connection refused/unreachable is a pass).

netProbe.description: scripted TCP dialogue (send/expect steps over one connection) for multi-step protocols

tls.description: force TLS; without it the connection is TLS only when the probed port is declared protocol: https (the primary port when port is unset)

expect_absent.description: regex the response must NOT match

read.description: bytes to read after this step, 1..65536 (default 4096)

sequenceProbe.description: Ordered steps run as one attempt, for race-condition targets: the core freezes and resumes the target between steps and reads the sanitizer reports and logs written during the attempt. `validate` checks that every freeze is resumed, that nothing runs in or connects to the target while it is frozen, and that the sequence asserts something.

attempts.description: attempts budget for harness flakes (default 1, at most 10)

min_hits.description: attempts that must hit for a sequence with a positive expect_sanitizer to pass (default 1, at most attempts)

container.description: run in this sidecar (a service.sidecars name) instead of the target; empty = the target

freeze.description: pause the target container (docker pause); never a sidecar. No options.

resume.description: unpause the target container. No options.

sleep.description: a fixed wait, in milliseconds (at most 10000)

expect_sanitizer.description: none: no sanitizer report may be written during the attempt; or { kind, frame }: a report of that bug class whose first stack has a frame matching the Go regexp frame. Needs service.sanitizer.log_dir.

frame.description: Go regexp matched against the frames of the report's first stack

expect_log.description: Go regexp that must match the target's container log written during the attempt

verifiedRun.description: One run: when, with which vulnsuite and on what host every listed state verified ok. Written by `vulnsuite stamp`, not by hand.

vulnsuite.description: the vulnsuite version that ran it

host.description: the container daemon's os/arch, e.g. linux/amd64

platform.description: the image platform, when it differed from host (the target ran under emulation)

cpu_flags.description: the requires.cpu_flags the host was checked to have
